pr.title: feat(cli): add new --worktree, with git-stk owning the worktrees it creates
pr.body:
`new --worktree` creates the branch in a worktree of its own instead of checking it out here, so your current checkout stays where it is. Location comes from `stk.worktreeDir`, defaulting to a `<repo>-worktrees` sibling, with branch names nested as real directories so `feat/a`'s basename still matches the branch tail.

git-stk records the worktrees it creates (`branch.<name>.stkWorktree`) and **owns removing them**: cleanup takes an owned one away when its branch lands - before deleting the branch, since git refuses otherwise - but never touches one you made by hand, and keeps an owned one that still has uncommitted work in it.

`repair` reconciles the marker both directions: it clears a stale one, and re-adopts an unmarked worktree sitting exactly where `new --worktree` would have put it (without which a lost marker would strand the directory forever).

<!-- git-stk:closes -->
Closes #283
<!-- /git-stk:closes -->

expected.description: The default worktree directory is derived from the current worktree's root instead of the main worktree, so `new --worktree` run inside a worktree nests the next one under it and repair looks for owned worktrees in the wrong place.
